heuristics: r-adding walk with r=2^24 behaves as a random mapping on negation classes (Teske 2001)

cycles of up to 64 classes are detected by a fixed 64-step checkpoint schedule and escaped from the cycle's smallest-u member, so merged walks stay merged; longer cycles have negligible rate (Bos et al. 2010; Bernstein-Lange-Schwabe 2011)
distinguished-point positions are independent of the table index
limitations: Analytic cost bound; no production-size execution.
Instruction counts are conservative scalar AArch64 estimates, not measured P-256 kernels.
Not a novel attack; textbook generic rho with the negation map.
